Besenyod Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Besenyőd, Hungary

Demolished. Besenyőd's Jewish population declined from 98 in 1840 to just 24 by 1880 (of 554 residents), recovering slightly to 40 by 1910 before falling again to 28 by 1941. In 1885, Besenyőd joined twelve other small communities (including Encsencs, Kisléta, Levelek, and Máriapócs) under Nyírbátor's Orthodox jurisdiction. County archives list 58 combined Holocaust victims from Besenyőd and Levelek. This cemetery appears on an 1870 cadastral map but was destroyed at an unrecorded time; village war memorials for both World Wars stand at the junction of Kossuth and Petőfi streets.
